disposition_reason: Table 4 prints element contents per 84 g tin for canned sardines in oil and tomato sauce from five Brazilian brands.

study.design: market survey of canned sardines, two packing media, five national brands
study.market: supermarkets, Campo Grande, Mato Grosso do Sul, Brazil
study.method: microwave HNO3/H2O2 digestion of about 400 mg drained meat, ICP-OES (axial)
study.qa: spike recovery 95-117% at 0.5 mg/L; no CRM

controls.outcome: Ba higher in tomato-sauce sardines (0.050-0.137 vs 0.020-0.048 mg/84 g); As did not depend on packing medium alone (p > 0.05); brand explained most As variation

unresolved: All concentrations are printed as mg per 84 g tin; conversion to mg/kg was not done because the paper does not print it.

Several lead means (e.g. 0.00007 mg/84 g, about 0.0008 mg/kg) and cadmium means (0.00002-0.00006 mg/84 g) are below the per-kg LOD in Table 3 once scaled to a kilogram (Pb LOD 0.0051 mg/kg, Cd 0.00063 mg/kg); detection at these levels by ICP-OES is doubtful. Not flagged per value because the per-tin unit prevents a direct comparison without computation.
Arsenic is total arsenic by ICP-OES, but hazard and cancer risk were computed as if it were inorganic.
Collection dates not reported; brand codes G, C, O, P, Pa kept as codes only.
